concept: A probability distribution describes possible outcomes and their likelihoods. Mean summarizes center; variance and standard deviation describe spread.
example:
# Customer order count X has this probability distribution:
# P(X=0)=0.2, P(X=1)=0.5, P(X=2)=0.3
# E[X] = 0(0.2) + 1(0.5) + 2(0.3) = 1.1
# E[X²] = 0²(0.2) + 1²(0.5) + 2²(0.3) = 1.7
# Var(X) = 1.7 - 1.1² = 0.49
breakdown: Expected value is a probability-weighted average.
Variance measures expected squared deviation from the mean.
Standard deviation is the square root of variance: 0.7 here.
practice: For X with P(0)=0.5, P(2)=0.5, compute E[X] and Var(X).
takeaways: Expected value need not be a possible outcome.
Distinguish variability in individuals from uncertainty in an estimated mean.

check.question: Which statement describes a probability distribution?
options: It specifies probabilities for possible outcomes of a random variable.
It proves that observed patterns are causal.
It always has a bell-shaped curve.
It is the same as a confidence interval.
check.explanation: Review the lesson overview and breakdown, then apply this distinction to the worked example.
